{{Short description|Change of the sign of a square root}}
{{About|conjugation by changing the sign of a square root|other uses|Conjugate (disambiguation)}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''conjugate''' of an [[Expression (mathematics)|expression]] of the form <math>a + b \sqrt d</math> is <math>a - b \sqrt d,</math> provided that <math>\sqrt d</math> does not appear in {{mvar|a}} and {{mvar|b}}. One says also that the two expressions are conjugate.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-22 |title=3.5.1: Resources and Key Concepts |url=https://math.libretexts.org/Courses/Cosumnes_River_College/Math_372%3A_College_Algebra_for_Calculus_(2e)/03%3A_Inverse_and_Radical_Functions/3.05%3A_Radical_Expressions_Encountered_in_Calculus/3.5.01%3A_Resources_and_Key_Concepts |access-date=2026-01-17 |website=Mathematics LibreTexts |language=en}}</ref>

In particular, the two solutions of a [[quadratic equation]] are conjugate, as per the <math>\pm</math> in the [[quadratic formula]] <math>x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac} }{2a}</math>.

[[Complex conjugation]] is the special case where the [[square root]] is <math>i = \sqrt{-1},</math> the [[imaginary unit]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Conjugate in Math - Surds, Complex Number, Rationalization |url=https://www.cuemath.com/numbers/conjugates-and-rationalization/ |access-date=2026-01-17 |website=Cuemath |language=en}}</ref>

==Properties==

As
<math display="block">(a + b \sqrt d)(a - b \sqrt d) = a^2 - b^2 d</math>
and
<math display="block">(a + b \sqrt d) + (a - b \sqrt d) = 2a,</math>
the sum and the product of conjugate expressions do not involve the square root anymore.

This property is used for removing a square root from a [[denominator]], by multiplying the [[numerator]] and the denominator of a [[fraction (mathematics)|fraction]] by the conjugate of the denominator (see [[Rationalisation (mathematics)|Rationalisation]]).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Conjugate in Math - Surds, Complex Number, Rationalization |url=https://www.cuemath.com/numbers/conjugates-and-rationalization/ |access-date=2026-01-17 |website=Cuemath |language=en}}</ref> An example of this usage is:
<math display="block">\frac{a + b \sqrt d}{x + y\sqrt d} = \frac{(a + b \sqrt d)(x - y \sqrt d)}{(x + y \sqrt d)(x - y \sqrt d)} 
= \frac{ax - dby + (xb - ay) \sqrt d}{x^2 - y^2 d}.</math>
Hence:
<math display="block">\frac{1}{a + b \sqrt d} = \frac{a - b \sqrt d}{a^2 - db^2}.</math>

A corollary property is that the subtraction:
:<math display="block">(a+b\sqrt d) - (a-b\sqrt d)= 2b\sqrt d,</math>
leaves only a term containing the root.
